# AGENTS.md

Hot Fuzz is a stereo fuzz/distortion + resonant wah effects card for the
[Music Thing Workshop Computer](https://github.com/TomWhitwell/Workshop_Computer),
running on a Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040). Integer-only fixed-point DSP, C++17,
no web editor in v1. See `README.md` for full design context.

## Build (firmware, needs Pico SDK)

```bash
export PICO_SDK_PATH=/path/to/pico-sdk   # or set PICO_SDK_FETCH_FROM_GIT=1 to auto-fetch
cmake -B build && cmake --build build -j4
```

Artifact: `build/hot_fuzz.uf2`. Flash by holding BOOTSEL and copying the .uf2
to the `RPI-RP2` drive.

Pico SDK 2.x required (CMakeLists pins 2.1.1). If `PICO_SDK_PATH` is unset and
`PICO_SDK_FETCH_FROM_GIT` is not enabled, configure fails — set one of them.

## Test (host DSP, no Pico SDK needed)

```bash
cmake -B test/build -S test && cmake --build test/build && ctest --test-dir test/build --output-on-failure
```

The test harness (`test/test_dsp.cpp`) compiles `dsp.h`, `svf_braids.h`,
`braids_resources.cc` against a desktop toolchain. It does **not** compile
`main.cpp` or `ComputerCard.h`. Run this after any DSP change — there
is no separate lint/typecheck step; `-Wall -Wextra` is the only static guard.

## Codegen: LUTs

`resources.h` is generated by `tools/gen_luts.py` and checked in for
reproducibility. Regenerate only if the wah-frequency mapping changes:

```bash
python3 tools/gen_luts.py > resources.h
```

Do not hand-edit `resources.h`.

## Architecture

Single-binary, two-core firmware.

- **Core0**: audio ISR (`ProcessSample` in `main.cpp`) at 48 kHz. Per
  sample: preamp → DC block → fuzz → DC block → envelope tap → SVF (wah) →
  crossfade → clamp. Fuzz rescaling uses a precomputed reciprocal LUT (8 KB)
  to avoid software division — the M0+ has no hardware divider. Use
  `int32_t` intermediates only; no `int64_t` on the audio path.
- **Core1** (`second_core_main`): LED updates (~100 Hz). Reads core0's
  published state via `c0_to_c1` struct. No inter-core commands needed.
- Binary is `copy_to_ram` (`CMakeLists.txt`) to avoid flash-cache jitter
  in the audio ISR. Keep ISR code RAM-resident.
- No flash persistence. Settings (fuzz type, switch position, auto-wah)
  reset to defaults on power cycle.

## Hard constraints (do not violate)

- **No `float`/`double` in DSP code.** CMakeLists enables
  `-Wdouble-promotion -Wfloat-conversion`; these warnings must stay clean.
  The M0+ has no FPU. Coefficients are Q15 (`int16_t`); crossfade is Q12.
- **No `int64_t` on the audio path** (slow on M0+). `int32_t` only.
- **Do not introduce a hardware divider dependency** in the ISR. Use the
  reciprocal LUT or shifts.
- Audio range is 12-bit signed (`-2048..2047`). Always `clamp_audio()`
  before output.
- `ComputerCard.h` is a vendored third-party library — do not edit it.

## File ownership

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `main.cpp` | Firmware entrypoint, both cores, UI/LED/switch logic |
| `dsp.h` | DSP primitives (fuzz, DC block, envelope, crossfade, clamp) |
| `svf_braids.h` | Braids state-variable filter (wah), vendored from Mutable Instruments |
| `braids_resources.{h,cc}` | Braids coefficient LUTs, vendored — do not edit |
| `resources.h` | Generated wah-frequency LUTs (`tools/gen_luts.py`) |
| `stmlib.h`, `stmlib_dsp.h` | Braids helper headers, vendored |
| `ComputerCard.h` | Workshop Computer card library, vendored — read-only |
| `info.yaml` | Workshop Computer card metadata (display name, controls, manual) |

## Gotchas

- **`info.yaml` documents switch behaviour.** It matches the code and
  `README.md`: Switch Up = fuzz + wah (Main selects fuzz type via 4 zones),
  Switch Mid = fuzz + wah blend (Main = dry/wet mix), Switch Down = wah mode
  (Main = manual sweep or auto-wah base freq; auto-wah toggled by
  double-tapping Down — Mid→Down→Mid→Down within 0.5 s, LED 4 flashes to
  confirm). Keep all three in sync if switch behaviour changes. Settings are
  not persisted — remove any mention of flash saves or factory reset if found.
- **CV1 connection is debounced (~11 ms)** to filter normalisation-probe
  transients that briefly override the Main pot. Preserve this debounce if
  touching CV handling.
- The `.gitignore` excludes `*.cmake` except `pico_sdk_import.cmake` — do
  not commit other generated cmake files.
- No CI, no pre-commit hooks, no remote. Verification is manual: build the
  firmware and run `ctest`. Re-run both before considering work done.
- `PICO_XOSC_STARTUP_DELAY_MULTIPLIER=64` is set deliberately — some boards
  fail to start without it. Do not remove.
